newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African Eastern Cape development plans due Wed.
newsitem.headline: S.African Eastern Cape development plans due Wed.

text.p: Trade and Industry Minister Alec Erwin on Tuesday said details of the long-awaited multi-billion rand plan to develop the under-developed Eastern Cape province would be unveiled on Wednesday.

He told the Western Cape branch of National Business Initiative, a private sector development organisation, that the project would include a new 1.5 billion rand road through the Wild Coast and a new port.
Erwin declined to elaborate, but Eastern Cape officials have been lobbying hard for the new port to be built at Coega, north of Port Elizabeth.
Gencor Ltd has said that it would like to build a 2.5 billion rand zinc refinery at Coega, but has warned that it could go elsewhere if government did not approve the development soon.
Erwin said that Cabinet would this week be asked to approve the building of a new port.
"It will be built and financed on a public-private partnership basis, so we are beginning to leverage in large projects," he said.
An investment conference would be held on November 7 for these projects and a wide range of others aimed at boosting development in the region.
The contract for the 1.5 billion rand road would be signed on Friday and would include a package of measures to include small and medium sized enterprises, which would be paid about 400 million rand.

"It will be financed very innovatively. It is the first time that this financing mechanism will be used in South Africa and it will be an interesting project that begins to attract foreign investment," Erwin said.
He said the project would be one of the several so-called spatial development initiatives (SDIs) being developed by his department to promote industrialisation and growth.
"None of this can happen overnight," Erwin said.

"This is a slow, determined process, we are not taking short cuts, there are no miracles, we are not offering massive incentives for things that won't come. We have to move through a careful but determined process."
